meta.scaleNote: game units per real metre; uniform, no compression
meta.axes: +X = east (toward Lake Michigan), -Z = north, +Y up. Matches the minimap (screen up = -Z), so the map is not mirrored.
meta.rotNote: All rot values are three.js rotation.y (radians). An object rotated by rot has its local +X axis pointing along (cos rot, -sin rot) in world (x, z). Building w is along local X, d along local Z.
meta.footprintNote: Footprints are CCW viewed from above (CCW in (x, -z)), open rings (first vertex not repeated). For THREE.Shape use (x, -z) then rotateX(-PI/2).
meta.source: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0 (https://www.openstreetmap.org/copyright); landmark heights from public references

landmarks.name: Willis Tower (233 S Wacker)
landmarks.desc: Black anodised-aluminium and bronze-tinted glass bundled tube: 9 square tubes of 22.9 m in a 3x3 grid, stepping back at floors 50, 66 and 90 so only two tubes reach the top. Two white antennas rise to 527 m. A glass ledge box on the 103rd-floor west face. It is the tallest thing on the map and anchors the west Loop.

landmarks.name: 401 N Wabash (river tower)
landmarks.desc: Silver-blue glass and brushed-stainless mullions. Three setbacks align with neighbouring cornice heights, then a slender spire. The plan is a rounded rectangle on the north bank of the river. No signage or lettering.

landmarks.name: St. Regis Chicago (Vista Tower, 363 E Wacker)
landmarks.desc: Three interlocking stacks of frustums, alternately tapering in and out, in blue-green gradient glass. A 2-storey open 'blow-through' gap near the top of the tallest stack. Three stacks of different heights (approx 363 / 259 / 179 m). Sits at the river mouth by Lakeshore East.

landmarks.name: Aon Center (200 E Randolph)
landmarks.desc: A plain square prism with no setbacks. Pale granite/white cladding, with vertical chevron-section piers running the full height that make a strongly striped surface. Flat top. The second-tallest bulk on the skyline, beside Millennium Park.

landmarks.name: Two Prudential Plaza (180 N Stetson)
landmarks.desc: Grey granite and silver glass. A square tower with notched (chamfered) corners and a stepped chevron/pyramidal crown topped by a 24 m spire.

landmarks.name: One Prudential Plaza (130 E Randolph)
landmarks.desc: A 1955 slab of limestone and aluminium with vertical strip piers and a flat roof carrying a tall broadcast mast (to 278 m). It sits next to Two Prudential.

landmarks.name: Crain Communications Building (150 N Michigan, ex-Smurfit-Stone)
landmarks.desc: A white-and-glass rhombus-plan tower whose top is sliced off by a steep 45-degree plane, giving the famous diamond-shaped sloped crown. It reads as a diamond from Michigan Ave. Lit white at night.

landmarks.name: Chase Tower (10 S Dearborn)
landmarks.desc: Light grey granite with dark glass. The long faces curve inward, so the tower tapers in a smooth concave A-line from a broad base to a narrower top. A sunken plaza on the south side holds a large mosaic wall.

landmarks.name: Chicago Board of Trade Building (141 W Jackson)
landmarks.desc: Art Deco grey limestone. Its pyramidal copper-green hipped roof is crowned by a 9.4 m faceless aluminium statue of a goddess holding wheat. It terminates the LaSalle Street canyon at its south end. Its clock and frieze are reliefs, not logos.

landmarks.name: Aqua (225 N Columbus)
landmarks.desc: A white concrete rectangle whose irregular, undulating balcony slabs make the facade ripple like water. Pale blue-green glass. There are 'pools' of plain glass where the balconies don't bulge. A wide podium has a rooftop garden.

landmarks.name: Marina City west tower (300 N State)
landmarks.desc: A 'corncob' tower: a cylindrical concrete core ringed by scalloped semicircular balconies, petal-like in plan. The lower 19 floors are an open spiral parking ramp with cars visible. One of a pair on the north bank of the river. A boat marina is at the base.

landmarks.name: Marina City east tower (300 N State)
landmarks.desc: The twin of marina_city_1, with the same corncob design. Use one model instanced twice.

landmarks.name: 330 N Wabash (AMA Plaza)
landmarks.desc: A Mies van der Rohe black steel I-beam mullion curtain wall with bronze-tinted glass. A flat rectangular slab, with a recessed double-height glazed lobby and a mechanical floor marked by a dark band. Its strict grid contrasts with Marina City next door.

landmarks.name: Carbide & Carbon Building (230 N Michigan)
landmarks.desc: Art Deco in black polished granite at the base, dark green terra cotta above, and a gold-leaf spire top. People often call it a champagne bottle. It has a slim tower on a stocky base.

landmarks.name: Wrigley Building (400-410 N Michigan)
landmarks.desc: Glazed white terra cotta that looks brilliant white and is floodlit at night. The south tower has a big four-faced clock tower and a wedding-cake lantern. A north annex is joined by a bridge. It stands at the north end of the Michigan Ave bridge.

landmarks.name: Tribune Tower (435 N Michigan)
landmarks.desc: Neo-Gothic grey Indiana limestone. Its crown is an octagonal lantern ringed by flying buttresses, like a cathedral tower. There are stone fragments embedded in the base. It faces the Wrigley Building across Michigan Ave.

landmarks.name: Chicago Theatre (175 N State)
landmarks.desc: A French Baroque terra cotta facade with a triumphal-arch window. It has a 6-storey vertical sign spelling C-H-I-C-A-G-O in bulb letters over a horizontal triangular marquee with chaser lights. The city name is not a brand, so the sign is OK.

landmarks.name: Merchandise Mart (222 Merchandise Mart Plaza)
landmarks.desc: A huge Art Deco limestone block, two city blocks long, on the river's north bank at the forks. Its centre tower is slightly taller. It has dense vertical piers and bronze spandrels, and is used as a projection-art facade. The L Brown/Purple line runs past its east end.

landmarks.name: Chicago Union Station headhouse (210 S Canal)
landmarks.desc: A Beaux-Arts limestone block with a Corinthian colonnade along Canal St and a barrel-vaulted skylit Great Hall inside. Tracks run beneath, west of the river south branch. The squat bulk is topped by a flat roof.

landmarks.name: Harold Washington Library Center (400 S State)
landmarks.desc: Postmodern red brick on a rusticated granite base, with huge round-arched windows. Its glass-and-steel green pediment roof carries giant green metal owl and seed-pod acroteria at the corners. A whole block at State and Van Buren.

landmarks.name: Art Institute of Chicago (111 S Michigan)
landmarks.desc: A grey limestone Beaux-Arts building with an arched portico facing Michigan Ave. Two bronze lions on plinths flank the steps; see art_institute_lions. To the east is the white, flat-roofed Modern Wing with a floating 'flying carpet' sunshade canopy, joined by a footbridge to Millennium Park.

landmarks.name: Art Institute bronze lions (pair)
landmarks.desc: Two green-patina bronze lions on granite plinths flank the Michigan Ave steps. The south lion stands 'in an attitude of defiance', the north one is 'on the prowl'. Each is about 2.4 m long on a 1.5 m plinth. Hero-scale props.

landmarks.name: Buckingham Fountain
landmarks.desc: A three-tier wedding-cake fountain of pink Georgia marble in an 85 m round basin. The central jet shoots to 46 m. Four pairs of bronze Art Deco sea horses stand in the basin. It sits in a wide crushed-stone plaza on the Congress Parkway axis. A good kaiju arena.

landmarks.name: Jay Pritzker Pavilion
landmarks.desc: A Gehry bandshell: curling, peeling ribbons of brushed stainless steel framing the stage opening. A steel-pipe trellis (lattice of crossing arches) spans the Great Lawn in front of it for the speaker system.

landmarks.name: Mirrored bean sculpture (AT&T Plaza)
landmarks.desc: A seamless, highly polished stainless-steel kidney/bean shape with an arched 3.7 m-high 'omphalos' underneath. Fully mirror-reflective, so use an env-mapped chrome material. It sits on a granite plaza. Call it generic, not by its trademarked name.

landmarks.name: Crown Fountain
landmarks.desc: Two 15 m glass-block towers facing each other across a 70 m black granite reflecting pool. The towers' LED faces show giant faces that 'spit' water. Only the north tower's footprint is used here; mirror it to the south (way 126945441).

landmarks.name: Navy Pier wheel (Centennial Wheel)
landmarks.desc: A 60 m Ferris wheel with 42 enclosed gondolas on a white A-frame support. Its spokes are lit with LEDs at night. It stands mid-pier on the south side.

landmarks.name: Navy Pier Festival Hall + Grand Ballroom
landmarks.desc: Long low brick-and-glass exhibition halls running down the 1 km pier. At the east end is the Grand Ballroom, a domed hall with a lantern and two flanking towers. The pier headhouse has brick towers at the west end. Pier deck: concrete with a promenade along the south dock.

landmarks.name: Soldier Field
landmarks.desc: A Greek Revival stadium with two long Doric colonnades (about 30 m) on the east and west sides. A modern steel-and-glass seating bowl rises inside, cantilevering over the colonnades like a 'spaceship'. The north end has an open plaza. It is surrounded by lawn and parking.

landmarks.name: Field Museum
landmarks.desc: A long white Georgia-marble Greek-revival temple: an Ionic-columned central portico with caryatid porches at the ends, on a raised base with grand north steps. Museum Campus lawns surround it.

landmarks.name: Shedd Aquarium
landmarks.desc: An octagonal Beaux-Arts marble building with a central octagonal dome and Doric portico facing west. Its glass-walled Oceanarium wing faces the lake to the east. It stands on the shore at the base of the Museum Campus peninsula.

landmarks.name: Adler Planetarium
landmarks.desc: A 12-sided Art Deco building of rainbow granite with a copper-green hemispherical dome and bronze zodiac plaques at the corners. A dark glass semicircular wing wraps it. It sits at the tip of Northerly Island causeway with a lake view of the skyline.

landmarks.name: Lake Point Tower (505 N Lake Shore)
landmarks.desc: A three-lobed (Y/clover) plan of curving bronze-tinted glass with dark mullions, on a park podium. It stands alone east of Lake Shore Drive at the root of Navy Pier.

landmarks.name: Franklin Center north tower (227 W Monroe)
landmarks.desc: Brown granite and bronze glass with stepped setbacks capped by a pointed spire cluster. Vertical piers. Has a Gothic-deco feel.

landmarks.name: 311 S Wacker
landmarks.desc: Pink granite octagonal tower with a cylindrical glass crown that glows white at night, like a castle turret. Next to Willis Tower.

landmarks.name: Richard J. Daley Center (50 W Washington)
landmarks.desc: A weathering-steel (rust-brown Cor-ten) slab with very long spans and few floors, set on a wide granite plaza. The plaza holds a 15 m abstract rust-steel sculpture.

landmarks.name: Chicago Cultural Center (78 E Washington)
landmarks.desc: A Neo-classical limestone block with two large stained-glass domes inside, faced along Michigan Ave.

landmarks.name: The Rookery (209 S LaSalle)
landmarks.desc: A red brick and terra cotta Romanesque office block around a light court with a glass roof. Hollow square plan.

landmarks.name: Michigan Avenue (DuSable) Bridge
landmarks.desc: A double-deck, double-leaf trunnion bascule bridge with four limestone Beaux-Arts bridge houses at its corners, each carrying a large relief sculpture. Steel truss leaves are painted grey-green. A riverwalk passes under it. The generic bascule-bridge model can reuse its leaves.

landmarks.name: Generic Chicago bascule bridge
landmarks.desc: A double-leaf trunnion bascule in dark-red or grey-green painted steel with a through-truss parapet and a small control house at one corner. The leaves can raise to 70 degrees. There are about 15 in the map, all instances of one model scaled by bridges[].length and width.

landmarks.name: Elevated L track segment
landmarks.desc: A riveted steel girder deck carrying two tracks with a third rail, on paired steel columns at the kerbs about 15 m apart. The deck top sits about 7 m above the street. Green-painted or rust-grey latticework. Tile along elevatedRail polylines (Wabash, Lake, Wells, Van Buren form the Loop). There are curve pieces at the 4 corners.

landmarks.name: Elevated L station (e.g. Washington/Wabash)
landmarks.desc: Twin side platforms on the elevated structure, with a wavy/rippled steel canopy (Washington/Wabash style) or a historic wood-and-tin canopy (Quincy style). Stair towers come down to the sidewalk.

landmarks.name: Chicago Riverwalk
landmarks.desc: A granite-paved promenade about 6-8 m wide along the south bank of the main stem, about 6 m below street level. It has stepped terraces to the water, cafe kiosks, planters and boat docks. It runs under each bridge. Use the riverwalk[] polylines.
